title: Backup and Recovery
subtopics: Recovery from Ransomware and Accidental Deletion
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terminology of Backup and Recovery.
Apply backup and recovery to a small synthetic example and identify evidence that supports the conclusion.
Identify a relevant limitation or failure mode and describe a safe defensive response.

content.intro: This lesson covers backup and recovery in the Data Security, Privacy, and Business Continuity track. It preserves the PDF's listed subtopics and develops a small, checkable defensive example. You will practice stating scope and assumptions, selecting relevant evidence, and describing what remains uncertain.
content.why_it_matters: A backup is not proven until a restore test succeeds, and a compliance checklist is not a substitute for understanding which rules apply. The specific focus here is backup and recovery; connect each subtopic to an observable check or a documented decision.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Backup and Recovery focuses on backup types and strategies; backup frequency and retention; offline and immutable backups. Define the system or data in scope, the expected behavior, and the consequences if that behavior fails. Then select a proportionate control and identify evidence that can verify both the normal path and an important failure case.

items.title: Backup Types and Strategies
items.text: Resilience is demonstrated by a tested restore or recovery exercise, not by the presence of a backup button. Document recovery-point and recovery-time objectives, dependencies, access to recovery credentials, and the evidence from the test.

items.title: Backup Frequency and Retention
items.text: Resilience is demonstrated by a tested restore or recovery exercise, not by the presence of a backup button. Document recovery-point and recovery-time objectives, dependencies, access to recovery credentials, and the evidence from the test.

items.title: Offline and Immutable Backups
items.text: Resilience is demonstrated by a tested restore or recovery exercise, not by the presence of a backup button. Document recovery-point and recovery-time objectives, dependencies, access to recovery credentials, and the evidence from the test.

items.title: Backup Access Controls
items.text: Authorization should be enforced for the exact resource and action on the trusted server. Start with least privilege, deny access by default, and test both allowed and denied paths across roles and tenants.

items.title: Backup Integrity Verification
items.text: Integrity means data and system state remain accurate and protected against unauthorized or accidental change. Identify trusted sources, validation checks, and evidence that a change was expected.

items.title: Restoration Testing
items.text: For restoration testing, define the expected behavior, the system or data affected, and the relevant trust boundary. Record a safe verification step and one limitation rather than treating a successful demonstration as proof of complete security.

items.title: Recovery from Ransomware and Accidental Deletion
items.text: Incident response follows the current organizational plan and coordinates analysis, containment, recovery, communication, and improvement. Preserve needed evidence, document decisions, and escalate actions that may disrupt business or safety.

content_blocks.title: Defensive example (synthetic data)
content_blocks.notes: This example uses synthetic values and has no network dependency. CodeLeaf displays it as instructional text; production does not execute arbitrary learner code.

content_blocks.title: Safety and verification
content_blocks.text: Data security combines classification, minimization, access control, encryption, retention, backup, recovery, and privacy-aware incident handling. Before attempting any live security test, obtain explicit permission and verify that the target and method are within scope. When a secure isolated runner is not available, treat the code as a local/synthetic example and do not run arbitrary content on production infrastructure.

content_blocks.title: Run, verify, and reset
content_blocks.text: Review the python snippet as a local calculation. If you choose to run this example, use Python 3 and synthetic inputs in a disposable local environment; compare the displayed expected output with what you observe. If the result differs, check the copied inputs and runtime version, restore the synthetic input, and repeat. No scan, external request, or production change is needed.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Backup and Recovery focuses on backup types and strategies; backup frequency and retention; offline and immutable backups. Define the system or data in scope, the expected behavior, and the consequences if that behavior fails. Then select a proportionate control and identify evidence that can verify both the normal path and an important failure case. Apply this to one controlled example, record evidence, and note an important edge case. Next, continue to the next lesson or revisit the prerequisite concept if a key term is unclear.

content.task: Create a concise, reviewable artifact demonstrating Backup and Recovery. Use synthetic data or a controlled local training environment only. Include the relevant syllabus subtopics (Backup Types and Strategies; Backup Frequency and Retention; Offline and Immutable Backups), state assumptions, show what evidence would support your conclusion, identify one failure mode, and recommend a defensive next step. Do not test systems outside written authorization.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use only a synthetic dataset, a disposable local lab, or an explicitly authorized system.
Include a clear scope/assumption statement and enough sanitized evidence for another learner to follow the reasoning.
Explain one limitation, edge case, or failure mode.
Recommend a proportionate defensive control and describe how to verify it safely.
hints: Write the expected behavior and test boundary before looking at a result.
Change one assumption at a time; compare results against the original synthetic case.
Record evidence and uncertainty separately, and select a proportionate protective action.
troubleshooting: The example is illustrative and should be reviewed against current platform/version documentation before production use.
If an output differs, check the input and runtime version; do not broaden the activity to an unrelated system.
Use only fake data and remove all temporary local artifacts when the exercise is complete.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one observation as conclusive proof.
common_mistakes.why: Security telemetry and tests cover only the cases they were designed to observe.
common_mistakes.fix: Corroborate important claims and document coverage gaps.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing a target without confirming authorization.
common_mistakes.why: A technical ability to reach a system does not grant permission to assess it.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic input or a local lab; stop if the approved scope is unclear.

common_mistakes.problem: Skipping the version and context assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Security controls and protocol details vary across implementations and deployment models.
common_mistakes.fix: Record versions, configuration, expected output, and the source used for verification.

summary: Backup and Recovery is best understood within its defined scope and trust boundaries.
Use relevant evidence and test both an expected case and a meaningful failure case.
Record uncertainty and choose a proportionate, authorized defensive next step.
